title: the MM2 letter R walk - the rat (ordinary and vapor), raven (ordinary, huge and giant), retch plant and rock reptile turns
audit_label: R812 MM2 letter R walk audit
audit_comment: THE MM2 LETTER R WALK - the ordinary rat and the vapor rat p. 105, the raven (crow) variant table p. 105 (the ordinary, huge and giant columns), the retch plant and the rock reptile p. 106; the R-FLIP round: the Letter R gap box flips to closed (23 closed, 14 open). SEVEN .lua defs ride the R791 data_files extension, registry 726 -> 733. The RStats 7x10 grid cross-checks every armor class, hit dice, bonus, avgHp, attack, xp, xp/hp, lair, move and magic-resistance cell; the per-def doctrine pins carry the settled reads (the ordinary rat and the ordinary raven 1/4 hit dice the flat-hp path reads - hdNum 0, avgHp 2, the ikiryo precedent; the huge raven 1-1 the hdNum 1 bonus -1 read - the buckawn precedent; the retch plant 5-8 the first-number 5 read - the quickwood precedent; the rock reptile the M-row V/400+7 xp with the L-row VI/600+9 riding as consts; the ordinary raven I/Nil the Nil-xp read - the phantom precedent; the vapor rat 6 (or special) armor class and 12/6/1 move the verbatim print cells; every Standard magic resistance 0 - the R155 class); the R812b repair note: the first cut carried the lair cells verbatim as 30%/25%/15%/10% and the preflight walked them bad 5 (the loader luaGetInt is a lua_isnumber-only coercer - a percent string reads 0), the bare-numeral read now pinned - the R639 repair flow, nothing landed, the same round number re-issued

tables.name: the ordinary rat to rock reptile stat grid
tables.audit_comment: THE R-GRID: the 7-row RStats stat grid (every armor class, hit-dice, bonus, avgHp, attack, xp, xp/hp, lair, move and magic-resistance cell of the seven letter R stat blocks, in print order - the ordinary rat and the vapor rat p. 105, the raven (crow) variant table p. 105 (the ordinary, huge and giant columns), the retch plant and the rock reptile p. 106)
col_comments: The armor class cells (the vapor rat 6 (or special) rides the verbatim print cell, firstIntIn 6)

The hit dice num cells (the ordinary rat and the ordinary raven 1/4 reads ride the flat-hp path - hdNum 0, the ikiryo precedent; the huge raven 1-1 reads 1 die; the retch plant 5-8 and the rock reptile 5 read the base 5)
The hit dice bonus cells (the huge raven 1-1 reads -1 - the buckawn precedent, the hitDice = hdNum + bonus/4 form; the giant raven 3+2 reads +2)
The avgHp cells (the floor(3.5 x hd + bonus) formula: the vapor rat 7, the raven giant 12, the retch plant and the rock reptile 17; the flat-hp 1/4-die reads carry avgHp 2)
The attack cells (the loader semantics: the retch plant Nil attacks floored at 1)
The xp base cells (the raven ordinary I/Nil reads 0 - the phantom precedent; the rock reptile M-row V/400)
The xp per hit point cells (the rat ordinary 1, the vapor rat 2, the raven huge 1, the raven giant 4, the retch plant 6, the rock reptile 7)

The in-lair percentage cells (the loader luaGetInt accepts only lua_isnumber strings, so the print 30%/25%/15%/10% cells ride as the bare-numeral 30/25/15/10 read - the R810 pech and pedipalp precedent; the ordinary rat and the retch plant Nil read 0)
The move cells (the ground move reads: the raven 1/1/3 of the multi-mode cells, the retch plant Nil reads 0)
The magic resistance cells (every Standard cell reads 0 - the R155 class)

  text = "Vapor rats appear to be nothing more than large, gray giant rats. Their habitat, however, includes areas not common to giant rats, for these creatures also dwell in and on the substantial cloud islands which frequently serve as the abode of cloud giants.\\n\\nIt is possible for vapor rats to alter the substance of their bodies and assume a gaseous form. In this condition they appear to be wisps of cloud or similar vapors. In normal solid state, vapor rats move very quickly and rapidly, are able to swim well, and are capable of burrowing rapidly through loose soil or the material of cloud islands. In their vaporous condition, they are able to direct their movement much as a ship would steer before the wind, and they are thus able to move from cloud to cloud around the sky.\\n\\nVapor rats are omnivorous, loving garbage and carrion, which is typical of all rats. While they do not seek treasure, there is a possibility that the remains of their meals will contain some items of value. If discovered in their lair, there is a 25% chance for each of the following treasure types to be there: J (1-4), K (1-4), L (1-4), M (1-4), N (1-2), C-type for gems, jewelry, and magic. If angry, hungry, or cornered, vapor rats will attack by scurrying in and delivering sharp bites. Whenever one is killed or seriously wounded, it gives off a small puff of noxious fumes. This gaseous release is the equivalent of a stinking cloud spell (q.v.), but it will affect only 1 individual if within 5-8 feet of the vapor rat. The rat always directs its release at its opponent, and the gas dissipates beyond the maximum distance shown above. Thus, while it is safe to stay these monsters from a distance, they are particularly dangerous in close proximity.\\n\\nWounded or seriously threatened vapor rats will always assume gaseous form. In such state, they can only be harmed by attack forms which cause their vapors to be destroyed. Such attack forms include very hot or magical fire, lightning, and exceptionally strong winds.",
}

As soon as any approaching creature which could threaten the flock is seen or detected, the scout or scouts will give warning cries, screen themselves, and maintain a safe distance while keeping track of the creatures and reporting events to the flock by means of raucous calls and, possibly, movements as well. Giant ravens are both pugnacious and easily trained (if raised from fledglings), and so are often used as guards and messengers.
